summary:
R4 remains the model to trust right now — 65% at +25.0u over its last 14 days, and its SP category leans hot across the board too (R1/R2 SP sitting at 58% on 14d with +5.6pts over baseline). That SP signal matters today because the slate is loaded with strong-side pitching mismatches, and the top of the board — NYM @ TBR — is a full four-rating consensus on TBR with R4 pushing the biggest delta on the sheet at +2.91. Jax over Hagenman is exactly the kind of SP-driven edge that's been printing, and TBR as a picked team is hitting 68% (74% strong, +19.0u) on the season, so this is the closest thing to a lock on the board.

Elsewhere, the model is in lockstep on several plays worth leaning into: SDP @ CIN is a unanimous fade of the Padres with all four ratings between -1.0 and -2.35, MIL @ CHC is a clean consensus against Milwaukee despite MIL's strong 64% team number (worth noting the model's going against its own favorite team here), and BAL @ COL is consensus-negative on Baltimore, which lines up with BAL's shaky 54% team record and -2.0u strong mark — a good spot to trust the fade over the team-loyalty bias. DET @ MIN is the other clean 4-0 consensus with real separation, R4 pushing +1.96, fitting the pattern of R4 leading the delta on every strong consensus play today. Where the ratings split — ATL @ WSN, STL @ LAD, SEA @ BOS, TOR @ CLE — deltas are all sub-1.0 and not worth forcing; those are pass or minimal-unit spots. Watch hitting category on any of these too: it's carrying a 3-game losing streak across every rating (R1-R4 all 3L), so don't let a hitting-driven signal override the SP/trends combo, which remains the best-performing pair at 57.2% (270-202) on the season.
